summary: Re-tested swipe-triggered active-dragon calendar tracking after E1 added onScrollEndDrag alongside onMomentumScrollEnd. Baseline sanity re-confirmed: Sif's column shows green + 'Sif' subtitle for 2026-07-16. However, the swipe-to-logan tracking STILL fails - and this time I proved definitively it is a REAL APP BUG, not a Playwright/automation-tool limitation. By inspecting react-native-web's ScrollView source (node_modules/react-native-web/src/exports/ScrollView/ScrollViewBase.js and index.js), I found that on the web platform, ScrollViewBase's internal DOM event handler only ever calls the `onScroll` prop (via handleScroll/handleScrollEnd) - it NEVER invokes onScrollEndDrag, onScrollBeginDrag, onMomentumScrollBegin, or onMomentumScrollEnd. Those props are silently dropped/no-op on web regardless of how they're triggered. I confirmed this live: using page.mouse.wheel to perform a genuine native horizontal scroll on the ScrollView DOM node, scrollLeft actually moved from 0 to 355 (exactly one column+gap, landing on logan's column - visible in the screenshot, 'logan' name rendered behind the modal), yet activeDragonIndex never updated (calendar still showed 'Sif' subtitle + green for 2026-07-16). This is airtight proof the bug is in the app's reliance on onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag for web, not a synthetic-event/simulation issue - a REAL user swiping on the actual deployed web preview would hit the exact same failure.

integration_issues.flow: Swipe Daily Overview horizontal ScrollView to 2nd dragon column then open calendar
integration_issues.issue: CONFIRMED REAL BUG (not a testing-tool limitation): on react-native-web, ScrollViewBase never fires onMomentumScrollEnd or onScrollEndDrag (verified in library source - these callbacks are accepted as props but never invoked in the web DOM event handlers, only onScroll is wired up). The app's activeDragonIndex state in app/(tabs)/index.tsx is only updated inside onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag handlers, so it NEVER updates on web no matter how the user scrolls (mouse drag, wheel, trackpad, or touch emulation). Live-verified: performed a genuine scroll (scrollLeft 0 -> 355, exactly landing on logan's column, confirmed visually), but calendar modal still showed Sif/green afterward.

react_native_issues.issue: onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag are no-ops on react-native-web; app must use onScroll (with scrollEventThrottle) to track scroll position reliably on web, or add a Platform.OS==='web' branch. Native (iOS/Android) behavior would work fine since RN's real ScrollView does fire these events - only the web target is affected.

action_items: Root cause found: switch activeDragonIndex tracking to use the `onScroll` prop (which IS implemented on react-native-web) instead of, or in addition to, onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag. E.g. add onScroll={(e) => { const idx = Math.round(e.nativeEvent.contentOffset.x / (columnWidth + COLUMNS_GAP)); setActiveDragonIndex(...) }} with scrollEventThrottle={16}, guarded/debounced so it doesn't over-render, OR use Platform.select to only rely on onScroll for web and keep onMomentumScrollEnd for native.

Verified via react-native-web library source (ScrollViewBase.js + ScrollView/index.js) that onScrollEndDrag/onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollBeginDrag/onMomentumScrollBegin are dead props on the web target - this explains why BOTH the original fix (onMomentumScrollEnd) and the follow-up fix (onScrollEndDrag) failed identically.
Re-verify baseline unaffected: confirmed Sif/2026-07-16 still green in calendar, no completion data mutated during this test.
critical_code_review_comments: onScrollEndDrag addition in app/(tabs)/index.tsx (lines 189-192) is functionally identical to the pre-existing onMomentumScrollEnd handler and does not fix the underlying issue because neither event fires on web via react-native-web's ScrollViewBase implementation.

This is worth flagging as a general pattern risk: any other place in the codebase relying on onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollBeginDrag/onScrollEndDrag for behavior tracking will have the same silent no-op issue on the web preview target.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The dragon-scroll-tracking bug is NOT a Playwright limitation - proven via react-native-web source code inspection (ScrollViewBase.js only wires up onScroll on web; onMomentumScrollEnd/onScrollEndDrag/onScrollBeginDrag/onMomentumScrollBegin are accepted as props but never invoked) AND via live reproduction (genuine mouse-wheel scroll moved scrollLeft to exactly logan's column offset, verified visually, but activeDragonIndex/calendar subtitle never updated). Main agent should switch to onScroll-based tracking (with scrollEventThrottle) for web compatibility, or Platform-branch the handler. Once fixed, retest by: performing page.mouse.wheel(deltaX, 0) over [data-testid='overview-columns-scroll'], confirming scrollLeft changes, then opening calendar and confirming subtitle shows 'logan' and 2026-07-16 shows red.
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: react-native-web's ScrollView (used for the horizontal dragon-column carousel on the web preview) implements onScroll fully (fires on every scroll tick and on scroll-end via a 100ms debounce timeout in ScrollViewBase.js), but does NOT implement onScrollBeginDrag, onScrollEndDrag, onMomentumScrollBegin, or onMomentumScrollEnd at all for the web target - these props are destructured into `...rest` and passed down to the underlying View/div but never actually invoked by any DOM event handler (confirmed by reading node_modules/react-native-web/src/exports/ScrollView/{index.js,ScrollViewBase.js}). Consequently, app/(tabs)/index.tsx's activeDragonIndex state (used to determine which dragon's calendar data to show) never updates on the web preview regardless of scroll technique (verified with a real page.mouse.wheel horizontal scroll that moved scrollLeft precisely to the 2nd column's offset). REPRODUCTION: 1) Load Daily Overview with 2+ dragons. 2) Perform any real scroll on [data-testid='overview-columns-scroll'] (wheel, drag, touch) that moves scrollLeft to the 2nd column. 3) Open calendar via overview-calendar-button. 4) Observe subtitle/colors still reflect dragon index 0 (Sif) instead of the now-visible 2nd dragon (logan). MITIGATION: Replace/augment the momentum/drag-end handlers with an onScroll handler (throttled via scrollEventThrottle, e.g. 16-100ms) that computes and sets activeDragonIndex from e.nativeEvent.contentOffset.x - this event IS fully functional cross-platform (native RN + react-native-web).
